name: Pleomorphic Rhabdomyosarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Soft Tissue Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of pleomorphic rhabdomyoblasts with eosinophilic cytoplasm and cross-striations on histology
Positive immunostaining for skeletal muscle markers such as desmin, myogenin, and MyoD1
Exclusion of embryonal and alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma subtypes by morphology and molecular testing
Absence of PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion gene typical of alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of pleomorphic rhabdomyoblasts with positive immunohistochemistry for muscle markers and exclusion of other rhabdomyosarcoma subtypes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular studies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging soft tissue mass with pleomorphic cellular morphology
searchTerms: fast-growing soft tissue tumor with varied cell types
rapidly enlarging mass with mixed cell shapes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of palpable firm tumor in extremities or trunk
searchTerms: hard tumor felt in arms, legs, or trunk
palpable firm mass on limbs or body

common.symptomName: Localized swelling and tenderness over tumor site
searchTerms: swelling and soreness over tumor area

common.symptomName: Restricted range of motion due to tumor mass effect
searchTerms: movement limitation caused by tumor pressure
restricted motion due to tumor size

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including low-grade fever and malaise
searchTerms: general symptoms like low fever and tiredness

common.symptomName: Weight loss associated with advanced disease

searchTerms: skin sores or ulcers over tumor
open wounds on skin covering mass

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression

searchTerms: breathing problems due to distant metastases

rare.symptomName: Pathological fractures due to bone invasion
searchTerms: fractures caused by cancer in bone

laboratory: Anemia of chronic disease in advanced cases
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous soft tissue mass with necrotic areas
CT scan for evaluation of metastases
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for desmin, myogenin, and MyoD1

distinguishingFeatures: Monomorphic small round blue cell morphology
More common in children and adolescents
Lack of skeletal muscle differentiation markers
Negative immunohistochemistry for myogenin and MyoD1
More common in older adults without rhabdomyoblastic features

redFlags: Rapid tumor growth with increasing size over weeks
Presence of distant metastases at diagnosis
references: WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours. 5th ed. IARC; 2020.
Parham DM. Rhabdomyosarcoma in adults and children: an update. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2001;125(1):6-10.
